what_its_for: Nimodipine is used to prevent and treat problems with blood flow in the brain that can happen after a certain type of bleeding in the brain called a subarachnoid hemorrhage (bleeding around the brain). It helps keep blood vessels in the brain from tightening up too much, which can lower the risk of brain damage.
how_to_take: Take nimodipine by mouth every 4 to 6 hours, exactly as your doctor tells you. If you are using the liquid form (oral solution), use the special measuring device or oral syringe that comes with it — never use a regular household spoon. Take it on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal. If you have trouble swallowing, ask your doctor or pharmacist about the liquid form. NEVER inject nimodipine into a vein — this can be life-threatening. Always swallow or take it by mouth only.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 60 mg (one capsule or the equivalent liquid dose) taken every 4 hours for 21 days in a row. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have liver problems. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it has been less than 2 hours since you were supposed to take it. If it has been longer than 2 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regularly scheduled time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store nimodipine capsules at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep them away from heat, light, and moisture. Store the liquid form in the refrigerator or at room temperature as directed on the label. Keep all forms of this medication out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice or eating grapefruit while taking nimodipine, as it can raise the level of this drug in your body and increase side effects. Avoid alcohol, as it can increase dizziness or lower your blood pressure too much. Avoid standing up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as this medicine can lower your blood pressure and make you feel dizzy or faint. Tell your doctor before taking any other blood pressure medicines, antifungal medicines, antibiotics, seizure medicines, or herbal supplements, as they may interact with nimodipine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: very low blood pressure (feeling faint, dizzy, or lightheaded); fast or irregular heartbeat; severe headache; chest pain or tightness; shortness of breath; swelling of your hands, feet, or ankles; unusual weakness; or signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or stomach pain. Also call your doctor if your symptoms get worse or you have any concerns about side effects.
when_it_works: Nimodipine starts working in your body within 1 to 2 hours after you take it. It is most important that you take every dose on schedule for all 21 days of your treatment, even if you feel fine. The full benefit of this medicine is seen over the entire 21-day course of treatment.
special_populations: Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects of nimodipine and may have a higher risk of dizziness or falls — use extra caution. People with liver disease may need a lower dose because the body processes this drug through the liver. Nimodipine is not recommended during pregnancy unless clearly needed, and breastfeeding mothers should talk to their doctor before using this medicine. This medication is not approved for use in children.
